title: The Story of a Kurdish General

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访几位商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、

sentences.en: Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 佐兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日要闻。

sentences.en: The Trump administration has ordered a full evacuation of the 1,000 American troops that
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府已下令全面撤离仍留在叙利亚北部的1000名美军，

sentences.en: still remain in northern Syria, as Turkey intensifies its bombardment of the Kurdish forces there.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，土耳其正在加强对当地库尔德武装的轰炸。

sentences.en: How is it that those Kurdish forces came to be seen as allies to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这些库尔德武装是如何被美国视为盟友，

sentences.en: and terrorists to Turkey?
sentences.zh: 却被土耳其视为恐怖分子的呢？

sentences.en: Monday, October 14th.
sentences.zh: 10月14日，星期一。

sentences.en: Ben, give us a sense of what's going on today, where you are.
sentences.zh: 本，给我们讲讲你那边今天的情况。

sentences.en: What are you doing?
sentences.zh: 你在做什么？

sentences.en: I'm in Erbil in northern Iraq.
sentences.zh: 我现在在伊拉克北部的埃尔比勒。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Middle East correspondent Ben Hubbard, on Friday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 周五下午，我与我的同事、中东记者本·哈伯德进行了交谈。

sentences.en: I'm waiting for permission from the Kurdish authorities here to cross the border into Syria so that we can go and cover the Turkish military incursion there.
sentences.zh: 我正在等待当地库尔德当局的许可，以便越过边境进入叙利亚，去报道那里的土耳其军事入侵。

sentences.en: You know, it started the other day with sort of shells flying across the border, a few airstrikes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，前几天局势就开始了，炮弹飞过边境，还有几次空袭。

sentences.en: Today, there was a large car bomb in the main city in this area where we usually stay and where we've stayed on our previous trips.
sentences.zh: 今天，在我们通常停留的这个地区的主城区发生了一起大型汽车炸弹袭击，我们之前的行程也住在这里。

sentences.en: It actually happened right down the street from this little fast food restaurant where we used to go and buy sandwiches.
sentences.zh: 它发生的地方离我们以前常去买三明治的那家小快餐店只有一条街之隔。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So that's scary.
sentences.zh: 那太可怕了。

sentences.en: We all the time see these images from the Middle East of things getting blown up.
sentences.zh: 我们总是从中东看到这些爆炸的画面。

sentences.en: But when you sort of recognize this place, it, you know, it brings it home a bit more than, you know, just kind of seeing some kind of destruction on the news.
sentences.zh: 但当你熟悉那个地方时，你知道，这比单纯在新闻里看到某种破坏更能让你感同身受。

sentences.en: How many times have you done this now, gone into Syria?
sentences.zh: 你现在去过叙利亚多少次了？

sentences.en: I've done seven trips into Syria since the start of the civil war.
sentences.zh: 自内战开始以来，我一共去过叙利亚七次。

sentences.en: My last trip was earlier this year, and that was after Trump had said that he wanted to pull the United States forces.
sentences.zh: 我上一次去是今年早些时候，那是在特朗普表示他想撤出美国军队之后。

sentences.en: At that time, there were about 2,000 American troops based in northeastern Syria.
sentences.zh: 当时，大约有2000名美军驻扎在叙利亚东北部。

sentences.en: And we have won against ISIS.
sentences.zh: 我们已经战胜了“伊斯兰国”。

sentences.en: We've beaten them, and we've beaten them badly.
sentences.zh: 我们打败了他们，而且打得很惨。

sentences.en: We've taken back the land.
sentences.zh: 我们收复了失地。

sentences.en: And now it's time for our troops to come back home.
sentences.zh: 现在是我们的军队回家的时候了。

sentences.en: The pullout of U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国从叙利亚撤军，

sentences.en: troops from Syria has America's allies bracing for more conflict.
sentences.zh: 让美国的盟友们为更多的冲突做好了准备。

sentences.en: President Trump spoke to Turkey's president on the phone yesterday and warned him not to
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统昨天与土耳其总统通了电话，警告他不要

sentences.en: mistreat members of the Kurdish community who are fighting ISIS alongside the United States.
sentences.zh: 虐待那些与美国并肩作战对抗“伊斯兰国”的库尔德社区成员。

sentences.en: So we wanted to go back and visit and see what this place, you know, what it looked like, how people felt, how they were planning for it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们想回去看看那个地方，你知道，看看它是什么样子，人们感觉如何，他们是如何规划的。

sentences.en: There was a lot of nervousness.
sentences.zh: 当时有很多不安情绪。

sentences.en: People didn't really know how it was going to affect them.
sentences.zh: 人们真的不知道这会如何影响他们。

sentences.en: And, you know, there was a lot of worry that it would destabilize this part of the country.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，很多人担心这会破坏该地区的稳定。

sentences.en: And there was this one particular person that I really wanted to meet.
sentences.zh: 而且有一个特别的人，我真的很想见见。

sentences.en: His name was Muslim Kobani.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫穆斯林·科巴尼。

sentences.en: And why did you want to meet him?
sentences.zh: 你为什么想见他？

sentences.en: So Muslim Kobani is the most powerful person in this northeastern corner of Syria.
sentences.zh: 穆斯林·科巴尼是叙利亚东北部最有权势的人。

sentences.en: General Kobani built his army in Syria with farmers, factory workers, and students.
sentences.zh: 科巴尼将军用农民、工厂工人和学生在叙利亚建立了自己的军队。

sentences.en: Members of an ethnic minority known as the Kurds dominate the militia.
sentences.zh: 这支民兵组织主要由被称为库尔德人的少数民族成员组成。

sentences.en: He is the head of the Syrian Democratic Forces, which is an umbrella group of a number of militias.
sentences.zh: 他是叙利亚民主军的领导人，这是一个由多个民兵组织组成的伞状机构。

sentences.en: The Syrian Democratic Forces, or SDF, led by the Kurds, had been the Americans' main allies in the fight against the Islamic State group.
sentences.zh: 由库尔德人领导的叙利亚民主军（SDF）一直是美国在打击“伊斯兰国”组织战斗中的主要盟友。

sentences.en: And this guy is the head.
sentences.zh: 而这家伙就是头目。

sentences.en: I mean, he is the guy that, you know, decides what these various militias under his umbrella are going to do and where they're going to fight and how they're going to deploy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他就是那个决定他麾下各个民兵组织要做什么、去哪里战斗以及如何部署的人。

sentences.en: Block by block, house by house, they became the foot soldiers who took the state out of the Islamic State.
sentences.zh: 他们逐街逐户地战斗，成为了将“伊斯兰国”赶出该地区的步兵。

sentences.en: He's involved in strategy and he's also the go-to guy for the United States.
sentences.zh: 他参与战略制定，也是美国的主要联络人。

sentences.en: A senior U.S.
sentences.zh: 一位美国高级

sentences.en: military officer told us much of the credit belongs to this man, SDF leader, General Muslim Kobani.
sentences.zh: 军官告诉我们，大部分功劳属于这个人，SDF领导人穆斯林·科巴尼将军。

sentences.en: Muslim Kobani stands right at the juncture of the United States, of Turkey, of the Kurds, of Syria.
sentences.zh: 穆斯林·科巴尼正处于美国、土耳其、库尔德人和叙利亚利益交汇的中心。

sentences.en: This is the guy that's kind of at the center of this whole storm that's just broken out this week.
sentences.zh: 他就是本周刚刚爆发的这场风暴的核心人物。

sentences.en: So tell me about the last time that you spent time with him.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我说说你上次和他在一起的经历吧。

sentences.en: So I wanted to meet him on our last trip because I wanted to talk to him and ask him,
sentences.zh: 我上次去的时候想见他，因为我想和他谈谈，问他，

sentences.en: OK, well, you know, you've spent this last number of years building up this partnership with the United States.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你知道，你过去几年一直在与美国建立这种伙伴关系。

sentences.en: Now the president wants to leave.
sentences.zh: 现在总统想离开。

sentences.en: What, how does it affect you?
sentences.zh: 这会如何影响你？

sentences.en: So we put in a message saying that we'd like to see him and that we were in town and we waited.
sentences.zh: 于是我们发了条信息，说我们想见他，我们就在城里，然后我们就等着。

sentences.en: And then we sort of gave up on waiting, weren't sure when it was going to come through.
sentences.zh: 后来我们放弃了等待，不确定什么时候能有回音。

sentences.en: We actually went off to do something else.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上已经动身去做别的事了。

sentences.en: And when we were on the road driving in the opposite direction, we got a phone call and said, well, if you want to see him, come now.
sentences.zh: 当我们开车往相反方向走的时候，接到了一个电话，说如果你想见他，现在就来。

sentences.en: So we promptly turned the car around and drove out to a base that they have.
sentences.zh: 于是我们立刻掉头，开车去了他们所在的基地。

sentences.en: And they sort of showed us where to park and brought us in and then took us into a little trailer with sort of some seats and carpeting.
sentences.zh: 他们指引我们停车，把我们带进去，然后带进了一个放着座位和地毯的小拖车里。

sentences.en: And I think it had a, you know, it had air conditioning and a TV, but nothing super luxurious.
sentences.zh: 我想里面有空调和电视，但没什么特别豪华的。

sentences.en: And there he was sitting there wearing camouflage uniform.
sentences.zh: 他就坐在那里，穿着迷彩服。

sentences.en: He was fairly modest figure, quite soft-spoken, didn't have sort of the bluster that you get from a lot of powerful military folk.
sentences.zh: 他是一个相当谦逊的人物，说话很温和，没有那种你在许多有权势的军人身上看到的虚张声势。

sentences.en: I noticed when I shook his hand that his palm was quite soft, which sort of taught me that he was not somebody who spends a lot of time,
sentences.zh: 我注意到和他握手时，他的手掌很柔软，这让我意识到他不是那种花很多时间，

sentences.en: you know, holding a Kalashnikov and firing at the enemy, but somebody who was involved in much higher strategic matters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，拿着卡拉什尼科夫步枪向敌人射击的人，而是参与更高战略事务的人。

sentences.en: And I sat across from him, asked him if I could record, set down my recording, and then we began the conversation.
sentences.zh: 我坐在他对面，问他是否可以录音，放下录音设备，然后我们开始了谈话。

sentences.en: Tell me about that conversation.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说那次谈话。

sentences.en: I mean, at that time, it was quite theoretical because Trump had said that he wanted to leave.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时这还很理论化，因为特朗普只是说他想离开。

sentences.en: And then a number of people in the administration had sort of talked him down and said, no, this is a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 然后政府里的一些人劝阻了他，说不，这是个坏主意。

sentences.en: And so, you know, his messaging was very much that, you know, we've had a very good relationship with the United States.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他传达的信息很大程度上是，我们与美国的关系非常好。

sentences.en: It was working together with the United States that we were able to get rid of ISIS in Syria.
sentences.zh: 正是通过与美国的合作，我们才得以消灭叙利亚境内的“伊斯兰国”。

sentences.en: You know, he sort of talked about it as in this partnership was kind of keeping the lid on things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他谈到这种伙伴关系时，说它在某种程度上控制住了局势。

sentences.en: But there was a lot of concern about sleeper cells and about remnants of the Islamic State that were hiding out and just sort of looking for their opportunity to come back.
sentences.zh: 但人们非常担心潜伏的恐怖分子小组，以及那些躲藏起来、寻找机会卷土重来的“伊斯兰国”残余势力。

sentences.en: I think he was quite concerned that if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想他非常担心如果美国

sentences.en: left, that would be a lot easier for them to do.
sentences.zh: 离开，他们会更容易做到这一点。

sentences.en: And Ben, what is it about this man that would cause him to be seen so differently by the Turks than by the Americans?
sentences.zh: 本，这个人身上有什么特质，会导致土耳其人和美国人对他的看法如此不同？

sentences.en: Well, part of it is that the United States history with Muslim Kobani is very short.
sentences.zh: 嗯，部分原因是美国与穆斯林·科巴尼的历史非常短暂。

sentences.en: The Turkish history with him is very long.
sentences.zh: 而土耳其与他的历史非常悠久。

sentences.en: And so we have to sort of go back and look at the much longer history, you know, of who this guy was and what he was involved in before he showed up as a partner, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须回顾更久远的历史，看看这家伙是谁，在他几年前以合作伙伴的身份出现之前，

sentences.en: with the Americans a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 他参与了什么。

sentences.en: So he's Kurdish for one.
sentences.zh: 首先，他是库尔德人。

sentences.en: The Kurds are, you know, one of the largest ethnic groups in the world that does not have its own nation.
sentences.zh: 库尔德人是世界上没有自己国家的最大的民族之一。

sentences.en: There are 30 to 45 million of them, mostly in Turkey, Iran, Iraq, and Syria.
sentences.zh: 他们有3000万到4500万人，主要分布在土耳其、伊朗、伊拉克和叙利亚。

sentences.en: They were promised their own state by Western powers after World War I, which they never got.
sentences.zh: 第一次世界大战后，西方列强曾承诺让他们建立自己的国家，但他们从未得到。

sentences.en: And so the current borders of the region were drawn and the Kurds were left in all these different countries.
sentences.zh: 于是该地区的现有边界被划定，库尔德人被留在了所有这些不同的国家里。

sentences.en: And so most of them have been interested in having some kind of Kurdish independence or an independent Kurdish state since that happened.
sentences.zh: 因此，自那时起，他们中的大多数人都对实现某种库尔德独立或建立一个独立的库尔德国家感兴趣。

sentences.en: In Turkey, there was a very strong effort by the state to try to quash Kurdish identity.
sentences.zh: 在土耳其，国家曾非常努力地试图压制库尔德人的身份认同。

sentences.en: The Kurds have suffered repression, mainly in education and political representation in the country.
sentences.zh: 库尔德人遭受了压迫，主要是在教育和政治代表权方面。

sentences.en: They would ban teaching of Kurdish language in schools and other forms of cultural expression.
sentences.zh: 他们禁止在学校教授库尔德语以及其他形式的文化表达。

sentences.en: And in the late 1970s, there was a reaction to this.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代末，对此产生了一种反弹。

sentences.en: There were a number of Kurdish activists who got together and founded something called the Kurdistan Workers' Party, also known as the PKK.
sentences.zh: 一些库尔德活动人士聚集在一起，成立了一个名为库尔德斯坦工人党（PKK）的组织。

sentences.en: Although banned, the Kurdish Workers' Party is supported by many thousands of Kurdish villages, especially the youth.
sentences.zh: 尽管被取缔，库尔德工人党仍得到成千上万个库尔德村庄的支持，尤其是年轻人。

sentences.en: Most are convinced it's the only way for them.
sentences.zh: 大多数人确信这是他们唯一的出路。

sentences.en: They became a military organization.
sentences.zh: 他们变成了一个军事组织。

sentences.en: They were basically an underground guerrilla organization that went to war with the Turkish state.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是一个与土耳其国家开战的地下游击队组织。

sentences.en: And they would attack Turkish army vehicles, army posts, sometimes Turkish civilians.
sentences.zh: 他们会袭击土耳其军队车辆、哨所，有时也会袭击土耳其平民。

sentences.en: The Turkish army would respond with raids and attacks on Kurdish villages.
sentences.zh: 土耳其军队会以突袭和攻击库尔德村庄作为回应。

sentences.en: And it was just kind of classic insurgency and counterinsurgency.
sentences.zh: 这简直就是典型的叛乱与反叛乱。

sentences.en: According to Turkish sources, up to 2008, the conflict between Turkey and the PKK resulted in over 40,000 deaths, including PKK members, the Turkish military and civilians.
sentences.zh: 根据土耳其的消息来源，到2008年为止，土耳其与库尔德工人党之间的冲突导致了超过4万人死亡，包括库尔德工人党成员、土耳其军人和平民。

sentences.en: And so when Turkey thinks about the Kurdish issue and when they think specifically about the PKK, this is what they think about.
sentences.zh: 所以当土耳其想到库尔德问题，特别是想到库尔德工人党时，他们想到的就是这些。

sentences.en: So when Turkey calls the Kurdish terrorists,
sentences.zh: 所以当土耳其称库尔德人为恐怖分子时，

sentences.en: they're referring to Kurds who attempted to stage a kind of uprising within Turkey to finally get the state that they believed they were owed.
sentences.zh: 他们指的是那些试图在土耳其内部发动某种起义，以最终获得他们认为自己应得的国家的库尔德人。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the PKK is certainly growing.
sentences.zh: 而且库尔德工人党确实在壮大。

sentences.en: It now claims 50,000 members fighting for an independent Kurdistan.
sentences.zh: 它现在声称拥有5万名成员，为建立一个独立的库尔德斯坦而战。

sentences.en: So in the midst of this insurgency and counterinsurgency that's tearing apart southeastern Turkey, the PKK spreads.
sentences.zh: 因此，在撕裂土耳其东南部的那场叛乱与反叛乱中，库尔德工人党蔓延开来。

sentences.en: You have operatives who leave and set up bases elsewhere in the region.
sentences.zh: 你有离开并在这个地区其他地方建立基地的特工。

sentences.en: You have Kurds from other countries who sympathize with the movement and join.
sentences.zh: 你有来自其他国家同情该运动并加入的库尔德人。

sentences.en: And this is where Muslim Kobani comes into the picture.
sentences.zh: 这就是穆斯林·科巴尼登场的地方。

sentences.en: And what does he tell you about his own role in this story?
sentences.zh: 他跟你说了他在这个故事中扮演什么角色吗？

sentences.en: Almost nothing.
sentences.zh: 几乎什么都没说。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: We don't exactly know what his real name is.
sentences.zh: 我们并不确切知道他的真名是什么。

sentences.en: I mean, he goes by the name Muslim Kobani, which is a nom de guerre.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他用穆斯林·科巴尼这个名字，这是一个战争代号。

sentences.en: Muslim is a nickname, and Kobani is the name of his hometown.
sentences.zh: 穆斯林是一个昵称，科巴尼是他家乡的名字。

sentences.en: When I asked him what his real name was, he told me it was Muslim Abdi.
sentences.zh: 当我问他真名是什么时，他告诉我叫穆斯林·阿卜迪。
